artifacts.summary: Confirms Stage 3.5 Dispatch Prep as the wiring point for model_flag, resolves all three required design decisions (lifecycle-only scoping, once-at-Stage-1/MT-1 threading, confirmed hard-mode MT coverage), and gives precise re-measured edit anchors in commands/orchestrate.md (4 insertion points, not 2) and skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md.

memory_candidates.content: skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md has a single canonical 'Stage 3.5: Dispatch Prep' shared stage (invoked from every Stage 4 single-task dispatch site, every Stage MT-4 multi-task per-task loop, and the Stage 3.6 team fan-out spawn loop) that owns clean_flag/effort_flag/lit_flag/hard_mode handling for every research/plan/implement dispatch. Auxiliary diagnostic dispatches (drift inspection, churn/divergence audit, blocker escalation) deliberately do NOT call this stage and use raw Agent-tool invocations instead. Any new per-dispatch context concern (like a model override) should be wired into Stage 3.5 rather than each dispatch site individually, and doing so automatically scopes it to lifecycle dispatches only, excluding the auxiliary sites for free.

commands/orchestrate.md threads command flags through BOTH a flat args: Skill-tool string AND a separate JSON delegation-context object at each of its two dispatch sites (multi-task and single-task) -- unlike commands/research.md, which only uses the flat args: string. When mirroring research.md's flag-threading pattern into orchestrate.md, remember to add the flag to both representations (4 insertion points across 2 dispatch sites), not just the args string.

parse-command-args.sh's MODEL_FLAG defaults to the empty string "" (bash), not JSON null -- unlike commands/research.md's prose which frames the unset case as 'model_flag = null'. Downstream consumers threading MODEL_FLAG through orchestrate.md-style commands should treat empty string, not the literal token "null", as the not-set sentinel.
